narrative: OMX30 opens into a bull regime (+5.9% above 200-MA, +2.6% above 50-MA) with strong overnight US momentum (+1.31% S&P, +1.60% NASDAQ) and modest European follow-through. However, technicals flash critical overbought warnings: RSI sits at 80.32, Stochastic at 91.5/93.4, and price is -0.1% from 52-week highs. ADX 71.2 with bullish DI bias confirms trend strength, but elevated VIX (+7.38% to 18.78) and US 10Y yields jumping +100bp to 5.048% signal rising rate/risk premium concerns. The 0.275% correlation signal is positive but masks divergence: Asia weakness (-1.26% Hang Seng, -0.70% Nikkei) and mixed European performance suggest selective strength rather than broad conviction.
morningBrief: OMX30 set to open +0.4% to +0.6% on US rally carryover and strong USD/SEK (9.983, +1.23%), benefiting exporters. Watch the 3180 level (50-MA) as initial resistance; support comes in at 3085 (lower Bollinger band). Industrials (Atlas Copco, Volvo B) should outperform on currency tailwinds and positive global manufacturing sentiment, but rising oil and yields create headwinds for real estate (refinancing pain) and tech (DCF compression). Banks (SEB A, Handelsbanken A) should see NIM expansion from 10Y +100bp. Critical risk: RSI 80.32 and Stochastic overbought combined with VIX spike signals mean-reversion potential—any profit-taking or risk-off macro shock could trigger 0.5–1.0% pullback. US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET is key intraday catalyst. Play the strength early but reduce exposure into any resistance.
